data.description:
## Summary

PR #378 ships the two-phase parallel bug-resolution pipeline (investigation phase + fix-application phase with ticket-scratch handoff) with structural tests only. The structural test (tests/skills/test-debug-everything-two-phase-pipeline.sh) asserts boundary-token presence and cross-file token coverage, but does NOT exercise the orchestrator-dispatch flow end-to-end.

## Gap analysis (Step 1)

A functional integration test would:
1. Mock the orchestrator dispatch surface (Agent tool stubs)
2. Run a Phase 1 sub-agent against a fixture bug, verify it writes fix-bug:investigation scratch + emits the 6-token compact summary
3. Run the orchestrator-level routing logic against the compact summary, verify it correctly classifies COMPLEX_ESCALATION / MANUAL_APPROVAL_NEEDED / FIXABLE / INVESTIGATION_FAILED branches
4. Run a Phase 2 sub-agent that reads scratch, verify it follows Path A normal vs Path A oversize-fallback correctly
5. Verify conflict-aware grouping in the orchestrator's Phase 2 dispatch

## Why deferred
- Non-trivial to mock the Agent tool surface
- PR #378 ships with structural coverage; functional gaps are bounded by the structural contracts
- A functional test belongs in its own dedicated PR with adequate harness design

Filed in response to PR #378 llm-review finding: "Two-phase parallel pipeline lacks functional integration test."
data.title: [debug-everything]: two-phase pipeline lacks functional integration test — only structural assertions cover the contract
